findings.problem: `expected_statuses = success_statuses or {200, 201}` uses truthiness rather than an explicit `is None` check, while the parameter is typed `set[int] | None = None`. An explicitly-passed empty set (`success_statuses=set()`, meaning "no status is a success") is silently coerced to the default `{200, 201}`, inverting the caller's intent. No current caller passes an empty set, so this is latent rather than live. The adjacent code in the same method uses explicit `is not None` for the analogous optional parameter (`if json_body is not None:` at line 231), so the truthiness form is locally inconsistent with the file's own established idiom.
findings.fix: Match the neighbouring convention: `expected_statuses = {200, 201} if success_statuses is None else success_statuses`.

intent_doc_match.note: The plan specifies which statuses cancel_download accepts but says nothing about how the default is resolved inside _request_json. The falsy-vs-None handling is an unspecified implementation detail, not an authorized deviation.

findings.title: cancel_download's transfer_id contract has no producer — slskd transfer IDs are never captured anywhere in the codebase
findings.problem: cancel_download(username, transfer_id) issues DELETE /api/v0/transfers/downloads/{username}/{id}, where slskd identifies the transfer by its own GUID. I traced every producer of transfer identity in this repo and none exists: (1) src/roonseek/schema.sql:341-353 defines `transfers` with `id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY` (a local SQLite rowid) plus username/folder_path/filename — there is NO column holding an slskd-side id; grep for `slskd_transfer_id`/`external_id` across src/ returns hits only in slskd.py/search.py for SEARCH ids, never transfers. (2) The polling parser `_inspect_transfer_status` (src/roonseek/pipeline.py:724-780) reads only `filename`, `state`, `directory`, and `bytesTransferred` from the slskd response — it never reads the per-file `id`, so the GUID is discarded on every poll. (3) The dataclass TransferStatus (transfer.py:33-39) declares an `id` field but grep shows it is never constructed outside tests/test_transfer.py:375. The pending caller confirms the mismatch: tests/test_jobs_api.py:659 asserts `fake.calls == [("alice", str(transfer_id))]` where `transfer_id` is the lastrowid from the local `transfers` INSERT (tests/test_jobs_api.py:~570-580). So the wired-up cancel path will send slskd a local integer like "7" where slskd expects its own GUID. slskd returns 404 for an unknown id; 404 is not in {200,202,204}, so _request_json raises TransferEnqueueError("...HTTP 404", "unavailable") — the operator's cancel appears to fail (or, per the 22-03 plan step, lands in cancel_failed) even though the DB-side cancellation is correct. This is a design gap the diff's isolated unit tests (which mock the transport and pass a literal string) structurally cannot catch. pending: confirm slskd's DELETE actually keys on the per-file GUID rather than accepting filename, and confirm whether phase 22-03's remaining steps add an id column + capture.

findings.title: success_statuses widening silently changes 202/204 semantics for existing callers if ever passed, and 404 is treated as a hard failure for an idempotent DELETE
findings.problem: The `success_statuses` parameter is keyword-only with a None default and `expected_statuses = success_statuses or {200, 201}` preserves the prior behavior exactly for enqueue_download and get_user_downloads — so this is a backward-compatible widening, not a break. Two secondary notes worth recording: (a) `success_statuses or {...}` falls back to the default when an EMPTY set is passed rather than rejecting every status; that is almost certainly never intended by a caller but is a silent-wrong-behavior trap if someone later computes the set dynamically. (b) cancel_download accepts {200,202,204} but not 404. For a DELETE, 404 is the natural 'already cancelled / already completed' response, and the acquisition cancel path is inherently racy — the transfer can complete between the operator's click and the DELETE. Treating that as TransferEnqueueError(reason='unavailable') means a benign race is reported to the operator as a cancellation failure. Note also that this client is deliberately outside the search-only guard (tests/test_transfer.py:388 asserts transfer.py must NOT reference assert_search_only_operation), so widening the accepted-status set here adds no new dry-run safety exposure — the DELETE verb is newly reachable, but that surface was already unguarded by design.
